title: This Snail Hunts Fish With Insulin, the Same Hormone Diabetics Use
subject: geography cone snail

scenes.text: A snail hunts fish using insulin. Yes, that insulin.
The geography cone snail lives on coral reefs and eats fish. Its venom was a mystery.
In 2015, University of Utah scientists found its venom is full of insulin, shaped to match fish insulin.
In tests, that insulin made fish sluggish in the water, and in a fish it made blood sugar plummet.
Then the snail stretches its mouth into a net and swallows the dazed fish.
Slow them down first. Then lunch.

description:
The geography cone snail hunts fish with insulin in its venom.
University of Utah scientists found it slows fish and crashes their blood sugar before the snail swallows them.
How would you hunt a fish with a hormone?
first_comment: A snail that hunts with insulin. What weird hunter should we cover next?
